newsitem.title: UK: Opraf clarifies subsidy breakdown for UK rail deal.
newsitem.headline: Opraf clarifies subsidy breakdown for UK rail deal.

text.p: The Office of Passenger Rail Franchising (Opraf) on Friday gave a detailed breakdown of the subsidy payable to Virgin Group which has won the CrossCountry rail service franchise.
Virgin will receive a first year subsidy of 112.9 million, reduced from 127 million in the 1996/97 financial year, it said.
This clarifies a rounded figure given earlier by Virgin Rail director Will Whitehorn in an interview, when he said the subsidy would be 115 million pounds.
Virgin and Opraf confirmed that the subsidy level will be eroded over the 15 year franchise term, with Virgin paying the government 10 million in the final year.
